paragraphs.source_en: The days when the Kampaku was away were exceedingly hard on the wives of the lords gathered in Osaka. Though they lived in great mansions fragrant with fresh timber, in truth they were being held as hostages. Some dressed themselves carefully and went to pray at temples. Most, however, shrank from the fierce heat and quietly secluded themselves indoors. With nothing to relieve her boredom, Taka-hime—the daughter of Azai Nagamasa who had married Kyōgoku Takatsugu—decided to visit her elder sister, Chacha-hime.

paragraphs.source_en: Chacha was both furious and resentful. Why did this uncle lay bare every secret of his heart? Had he been some weak and insignificant man whose woman had been taken by one stronger than himself, such conduct would not have been surprising. But how could such a thing exist between an uncle and his niece? Why could her uncle not bury such feelings deep within himself and force himself to obey His Lordship the Kampaku?
